answer: A stake-bonded reputation market works: each agent locks a bond before trading, and peers can slash it on proof of duplicate or fraudulent behavior. Minting a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds, while honest agents get theirs back plus fees. Reputation also decays unless the agent keeps doing verifiable work — like a prospector who must keep digging through shale to prove the opal is real, not merely claim a whole island of gems. Each new identity starts at zero trust and must pay again, so Sybils are expensive to create and worthless to abandon.
